PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible
Video Generation

   Harold Haodong Chen, Rui Peng, Lingteng Qiu,    Kejie Qiu, Chao Xu, Zilong Dong    HKUST & Alibaba Token Hub    Alibaba Group*Work done at ATH@Alibaba Group, †Corresponding author https://haroldchen19.github.io/PhysOPSD-site https://github.com/aigc3d/PhysOPSD
Abstract

While modern video generative models achieve remarkable visual fidelity, they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions. Targeted post-training is crucial, yet supervised fine-tuning suffers from offline state mismatch, and reinforcement learning is hindered by sparse, ill-defined physical reward functions. On-Policy (Self-)Distillation (OPSD) reconciles on-policy rollouts with dense corrective feedback, shifting the core challenge to designing effective privileged context. However, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts are inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos heavily entangle physical laws with visual appearance without parametric control. To this end, we propose PhysOPSD, introducing executable code as privileged physical context for video generation. Unlike static visual observations, executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Powered by PhysOPSD-Engine, we translate real-world physical scenarios into verifiable simulation programs. PhysOPSD then incorporates (i) dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside (ii) controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose causal dynamic shifts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming SFT and RL baselines with only 33K samples, while preserving general video generation quality.

1 Introduction

Recent video generation models [40, 10, 15, 1] have made impressive strides in visual fidelity and temporal coherence, yet they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions [28, 2, 3]. Targeted post-training has thus emerged as a vital route to reinforce physical capabilities beyond pre-training [18, 32]. However, existing paradigms involve clear trade-offs: ➀ supervised fine-tuning (SFT) offers dense supervision [42, 29, 17, 49], but operates on offline data that mismatches the states visited during inference; ➁ reinforcement learning (RL) optimizes directly over on-policy rollouts [14, 8, 12], yet suffers from sparse, ill-defined rewards and credit-assignment bottlenecks.

Recent ➂ on-policy distillation (OPD) [22, 34] provides a natural middle ground by querying a teacher for dense supervision on student-visited rollout states. Building upon this, on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) [50] further removes the need for an external teacher by casting the same model into asymmetric roles: the student acts on inference-time inputs, while the teacher accesses additional privileged context to supervise the student rollouts. The central question of OPSD therefore becomes how to leverage extra information to turn the same model into a stronger self-teacher, as shown in Figure 2 (a). An effective privileged context should directly expose the information required by the target capability and reliably enhance teacher predictions on student rollout states. This principle has shown strong promise in language reasoning via ground-truth answers and rationales [50, 31, 47], as well as in image generation via target-image multimodal representations [13].

Extending this paradigm to video generation, however, is far less straightforward, as the primary bottleneck lies in modeling physically plausible dynamics, a capability that also defies evaluation by standard reward models [18, 42, 3]. Yet, designing effective privileged context remains non-trivial: text expansion provides richer descriptions but remains fundamentally declarative, whereas real reference videos capture complete dynamics but heavily entangle them with irrelevant appearance, identity, and background clutter without controllable structure (Figure 2 (b)). These bottlenecks lead to our core research question:

To answer this question, we introduce PhysOPSD, which proposes executable code as privileged physical context for video generation OPSD. Our key insight is that an executable physical scene instantiates an editable world rather than a fixed visual outcome. This executability inherently provides two structural properties absent in raw video data: ❶ abstraction, the ability to express dynamics across varying information densities; and ❷ controllability, the ability to isolate and systematically perturb underlying physical parameters. To operationalize this insight, we first develop PhysOPSD-Engine, which converts diverse real-world scenarios into verifiable simulation code and renders synchronized physical drafts via a coding agent.

PhysOPSD then systematically translates these two properties into OPSD: ♣ dual-level physical privilege exploits abstraction by pairing dense drafts with abstract drafts, establishing an intermediate physical information bottleneck to bridge the privilege gap and prevent appearance shortcuts; ♠ controlled physical variation exploits controllability by altering specific physical parameters across paired scenes with shared rollout noise, explicitly supervising how physical shifts dictate dynamic outcomes. By internalizing structured code privilege through on-policy self-distillation, PhysOPSD empowers base video generators to generate more physically plausible dynamics and stable interactions directly from text prompts.

To summarize, this work contributes threefold:

  • •

    We propose code as privileged physical context for video generation, and introduce PhysOPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework incorporating dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap and controlled physical variation to capture causal dynamic shifts.

  • •

    We develop PhysOPSD-Engine to translate real-world physical scenarios into verifiable and controllable simulation programs, and construct PhysOPSD-3K, an executable physical scene dataset featuring multi-abstraction drafts and paired physical variants.

  • •

    Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD consistently improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming prior SFT and RL baselines with only a small fraction of their training data, without compromising general generation quality.

2 Related Work

On-Policy Distillation.

On-policy distillation (OPD) mitigates train-test distribution shifts by supervising the student directly on its self-generated states with dense feedback [22, 34]. This paradigm has been applied to consolidate domain experts in language models such as MOPD [27], fuse visual capabilities in diffusion and flow models [20, 7], and optimize sampling trajectories in video generation [9]. To eliminate the reliance on external teachers, on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) constructs a stronger self-teacher from the same model under asymmetric privileged information [50]. While ground-truth solutions and rationales serve as privileged context in language reasoning [50, 31, 47], D-OPSD [13] employs target-image multimodal representations to tune few-step image diffusion models. For video models, OPSD-V [26] replaces older KV-cache history with real video frames to mitigate long-horizon drift in few-step autoregressive (AR) generators. Unlike OPSD-V, which focuses on causal AR cache stabilization, PhysOPSD explores on-policy self-distillation for general video generation, introducing executable code as privileged physical context.

Code-for-Vision.

Empowered by modern foundational vision-language models (VLMs) [33, 37], executable code is increasingly utilized for visual scene synthesis and understanding. Early efforts such as 3D-GPT [35] synthesize Blender scripts to procedurally build 3D environments [16]. Recent studies further leverage coding agents for programmatic visual reconstruction, editing, and quantitative physical reasoning [48, 21, 36, 41]. More recently, researchers have explored coding agents to assist visual generation by delegating spatiotemporal processes to code execution [6], either as physics-aware drafts in Blender [19] or cinematic previsualizations in Three.js [23]. While existing generative approaches largely seek to replace part of generative modeling with coding agent capabilities, PhysOPSD explores how executable code can empower the generative model itself.

3 Preliminary: Problem Formulation

Modern video diffusion models [40, 10, 30] are predominantly formulated via flow matching [25], parameterizing a time-dependent velocity field:

d​𝐱td​t=𝐯𝜽​(𝐱t,t,𝐩),\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}_{t}}{\mathrm{d}t}=\mathbf{v}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{t},t,\mathbf{p}), (1)

where 𝐱t\mathbf{x}_{t} denotes the video latent at continuous timestep t∈[0,1]t\in[0,1], 𝐩\mathbf{p} is the text prompt, and 𝐯𝜽\mathbf{v}_{\bm{\theta}} represents the neural velocity predictor with parameters 𝜽\bm{\theta}. Starting from Gaussian noise 𝐱1∼𝒩⁡(𝟎,𝐈)\mathbf{x}_{1}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}), a video is generated over a discrete schedule 1=tK>tK−1>⋯>t0=01=t_{K}>t_{K-1}>\dots>t_{0}=0 via a numerical ODE solver Φ\Phi:

𝐱tk−1=Φ⁡(𝐱tk,tk,tk−1,𝐮k),with ​𝐮k=𝐯𝜽​(𝐱tk,tk,𝐩).\mathbf{x}_{t_{k-1}}=\Phi(\mathbf{x}_{t_{k}},t_{k},t_{k-1},\mathbf{u}^{k}),\quad\text{with }\mathbf{u}^{k}=\mathbf{v}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{t_{k}},t_{k},\mathbf{p}). (2)

This iterative integration yields the full generative trajectory that characterizes the model’s rollout behavior.

On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) optimizes this generative process by querying a privileged self-teacher directly along the student’s own rollout states. Formally, let 𝐜S\mathbf{c}^{S} denote the student condition available at inference (e.g., prompt 𝐩\mathbf{p}), and 𝐜T\mathbf{c}^{T} the privileged teacher condition augmented with additional task-specific context. During training, the student first samples an on-policy rollout trajectory:

𝝉S={𝐱tKS,𝐱tK−1S,…,𝐱t0S}∼𝒢𝜽​(𝐜S).\bm{\tau}^{S}=\{\mathbf{x}_{t_{K}}^{S},\mathbf{x}_{t_{K-1}}^{S},\dots,\mathbf{x}_{t_{0}}^{S}\}\sim\mathcal{G}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{c}^{S}). (3)

At each student-visited state (𝐱tkS,tk)(\mathbf{x}_{t_{k}}^{S},t_{k}), student and teacher predict their respective velocities:

𝐮Sk=𝐯𝜽​(𝐱tkS,tk,𝐜S),𝐮Tk=𝐯𝜽¯​(𝐱tkS,tk,𝐜T),\mathbf{u}_{S}^{k}=\mathbf{v}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{t_{k}}^{S},t_{k},\mathbf{c}^{S}),\qquad\mathbf{u}_{T}^{k}=\mathbf{v}_{\bar{\bm{\theta}}}(\mathbf{x}_{t_{k}}^{S},t_{k},\mathbf{c}^{T}), (4)

where 𝜽¯\bar{\bm{\theta}} denotes the teacher parameters, instantiated as an EMA copy of 𝜽\bm{\theta}. The student is then optimized by velocity matching over its self-generated rollout trajectory:

ℒOPSD=𝔼𝝉S∼𝒢𝜽​(𝐜S)​[1K​∑k=1K‖𝐮Sk−sg⁡(𝐮Tk)‖22],\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPSD}}=\mathbb{E}_{\bm{\tau}^{S}\sim\mathcal{G}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{c}^{S})}\left[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left\|\mathbf{u}_{S}^{k}-\operatorname{sg}(\mathbf{u}_{T}^{k})\right\|_{2}^{2}\right], (5)

where sg⁡(⋅)\operatorname{sg}(\cdot) is the stop-gradient operator. Crucially, the privileged context modifies only the teacher’s conditioning, leaving the student’s rollout states and inference behavior unaltered. The effectiveness of OPSD therefore hinges on whether the privileged context reliably improves teacher predictions on student-visited states.

4 PhysOPSD

4.1 Overview

OPSD relies on privileged context that reliably improves self-teacher predictions along student rollout states. In modeling physical dynamics, however, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts remain inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos merely capture entangled visual observations.

Executable Code as Privileged Context.

PhysOPSD bridges this gap by introducing executable code as privileged physical context, as shown in Figure 3. Unlike static text or video observations, an executable program explicitly specifies physical laws, object states, and dynamic parameters within an editable simulation, thereby uniquely providing explicit parametric control. To operationalize this, PhysOPSD-Engine first translates real-world physical references 𝐕ref\mathbf{V}^{\mathrm{ref}} into an executable program 𝒫\mathcal{P}. Simulating 𝒫\mathcal{P} in backend ℰ\mathcal{E} yields a visual physical draft 𝐝=ℰ⁡(𝒫)\mathbf{d}=\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{P}) and a grounded target prompt 𝐩=Describe⁡(𝒫,𝐝)\mathbf{p}=\operatorname{Describe}(\mathcal{P},\mathbf{d}). Here, code 𝒫\mathcal{P} generates the underlying physical dynamics, while the rendered visual draft 𝐝\mathbf{d} conditions the self-teacher.

Structured Physical Supervision.

PhysOPSD builds upon an omni video generator 𝐯𝜽​(𝐱t,t,𝐩,𝐝)\mathbf{v}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{t},t,\mathbf{p},\mathbf{d}), where 𝐝=∅\mathbf{d}=\emptyset denotes text-only conditioned generation. Rather than treating 𝐝\mathbf{d} as a static condition, PhysOPSD leverages two intrinsic properties of executable code:

  • ❶

    Abstraction: synthesizing dense drafts 𝐝dense\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}} and abstract drafts 𝐝abs\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}} to establish a stepped hierarchy (𝐝dense→𝐝abs→𝐩\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\to\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}}\to\mathbf{p}) that smooths the privilege gap;

  • ❷

    Controllability: perturbing physical parameters ϕ\bm{\phi} across paired scenes with shared rollout noise to capture causal dynamic shifts.

The subsequent Section 4.2 details PhysOPSD-Engine and PhysOPSD-3K, while Sections 4.3.1 and 4.3.2 elaborate the structured self-distillation mechanisms of PhysOPSD.

4.2 Executable Physical Context Engine

To systematically synthesize verifiable and controllable privileged physical context, we develop PhysOPSD-Engine, an agentic pipeline that translates real-world physical references into executable scene programs and rendered physical drafts.

Reference-Guided Scene Construction.

To seed simulations with natural diversity, PhysOPSD-Engine ingests real-world physical scenarios from WISA [42] and public video collections. Rather than attempting to simulate arbitrary physical phenomena, the physical scope is deliberately restricted to simulation-groundable physical dynamics, categorized into three domains: (I) rigid-body and contact dynamics, (II) elastic and deformable solid mechanics, and (III) fluid dynamics. Phenomena such as turbulent gas diffusion or thermodynamic phase shifts are excluded due to numerical instability and the difficulty of isolating causal physical parameters in standard simulators.

Given a reference video 𝐕ref\mathbf{V}^{\mathrm{ref}}, a coding agent 𝒜\mathcal{A} then extracts the dominant physical event and formulates a structured physical scene specification:

𝒮=(𝒪,𝒳0,𝚽,ℰ,𝒞),\mathcal{S}=(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{X}_{0},\bm{\Phi},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{C}), (6)

where 𝒪\mathcal{O} defines object geometries, 𝒳0\mathcal{X}_{0} specifies initial kinetic states, 𝚽\bm{\Phi} collects physical properties (e.g., friction, elasticity, mass), ℰ\mathcal{E} indicates interaction mechanisms, and 𝒞\mathcal{C} configures the camera trajectory. The coding agent then compiles 𝒮\mathcal{S} into an executable simulation program 𝒫=𝒜⁡(𝒮)\mathcal{P}=\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}). Standard simulation backends such as MuJoCo [39], Genesis [38], and Blender [4] are employed purely for their deterministic contact solvers and numerical stability, without asserting the superiority of any specific engine. Crucially, the governing principle is to reconstruct the physical scenario rather than visually reproduce the reference video: geometries and textures are simplified as long as the underlying physical mechanics are faithfully instantiated.

Execution-Guided Verification.

The synthesized program 𝒫\mathcal{P} is then refined through an iterative execution-observation-revision loop. Rather than optimizing for pixel-level trajectory similarity to 𝐕ref\mathbf{V}^{\mathrm{ref}}, verification enforces four strict criteria:

  • •

    Execution validity, ensuring code executes and renders without runtime divergence;

  • •

    Physical validity, verifying that dynamic events emerge from simulation mechanics rather than hard-coded keyframe animations;

  • •

    Visual observability, confirming that primary dynamic interactions are clearly visible within the viewport;

  • •

    Parameter controllability, ensuring that systematically perturbing key physical parameters produces physically consistent and observable dynamic responses;

Once verified, the target prompt is grounded directly on the executed outcome, 𝐩=Describe⁡(𝒮,𝐝)\mathbf{p}=\operatorname{Describe}(\mathcal{S},\mathbf{d}), guaranteeing semantic and causal alignment across 𝐩↔𝒫↔𝐝\mathbf{p}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{P}\leftrightarrow\mathbf{d}.

PhysOPSD-3K Dataset.

Using PhysOPSD-Engine, we further construct PhysOPSD-3K, an executable physical scene dataset for video generation. Each sample is represented as a structured tuple:

𝒟i={𝐩i,𝒫i,𝐝i,ℳi},\mathcal{D}_{i}=\{\mathbf{p}_{i},\mathcal{P}_{i},\mathbf{d}_{i},\mathcal{M}_{i}\}, (7)

where 𝒫i\mathcal{P}_{i} is the executable program, 𝐝i\mathbf{d}_{i} is the rendered visual draft, 𝐩i\mathbf{p}_{i} is the grounded prompt, and ℳi\mathcal{M}_{i} denotes structured metadata detailing physical parameters and execution configurations. Unlike static video collections, this executable formulation endows PhysOPSD-3K with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Encompassing the base scenes alongside their derived multi-abstraction drafts and parameter-controlled variants, PhysOPSD-3K comprises 33K total instances. We next detail how these structured properties are translated into self-distillation.

4.3 Structured Physical Self-Distillation

Building upon the executable formulation, PhysOPSD further translates code abstraction into ♣ dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap, and leverages controllability via ♠ controlled physical variation to supervise causal dynamic shifts, as illustrated in Figure 4.

4.3.1 Dual-Level Physical Privilege

Directly distilling from a dense physical draft 𝐝dense\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}} to a text-only student may incur two fundamental obstacles: (i) an excessively wide privilege gap that impedes knowledge internalization, and (ii) the risk of geometric shortcuts where the teacher overfits to explicit geometry rather than abstracting causal dynamics. We thus introduce an abstract physical draft 𝐝abs\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}} as an intermediate physical information bottleneck, isolating motion and contact topology while filtering out fine-grained visual details.

Privilege Construction.

From a single scene program 𝒫\mathcal{P}, the simulation backend ℰ\mathcal{E} renders physical drafts across distinct information densities:

  • ➀

    Dense Draft 𝐝dense\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}}: preserves complete surface geometry, collision contacts, dynamic interactions, and continuous spatiotemporal evolution.

  • ➁

    Abstract Draft 𝐝abs\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}}: retains coarse object-level motion, spatial trajectories, and contact events via simplified primitives, largely stripping appearance details.

These contexts define three hierarchical conditioning levels 𝐜(ℓ)\mathbf{c}^{(\ell)} for ℓ∈{0,1,2}\ell\in\{0,1,2\}:

𝐜(0)=𝐩,𝐜(1)=(𝐩,𝐝abs),𝐜(2)=(𝐩,𝐝dense),\mathbf{c}^{(0)}=\mathbf{p},\quad\mathbf{c}^{(1)}=(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}}),\quad\mathbf{c}^{(2)}=(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}}), (8)

where 𝐜(0)\mathbf{c}^{(0)} corresponds strictly to the deployment-time text-only condition.

Distillation Formulation.

PhysOPSD then establishes a stepped distillation hierarchy across adjacent information levels, 𝐜(2)→𝐜(1)→𝐜(0)\mathbf{c}^{(2)}\to\mathbf{c}^{(1)}\to\mathbf{c}^{(0)}: ➀ Dense-to-Abstract (ℓ=1\ell=1), where the student rolls out on-policy under 𝐜(1)\mathbf{c}^{(1)} and the teacher supervises under 𝐜(2)\mathbf{c}^{(2)} to guide motion synthesis under reduced structural cues; ➁ Abstract-to-Text (ℓ=0\ell=0), where the student rolls out under inference-time text 𝐜(0)\mathbf{c}^{(0)} and the teacher provides corrective supervision under 𝐜(1)\mathbf{c}^{(1)}, serving as the primary pathway for directly boosting text-to-video physical fidelity. Both transitions are optimized via a unified dual-level objective:

ℒdual=𝔼ℓ∼P⁡(ℓ)​[ℒOPSD​(𝐜(ℓ),𝐜(ℓ+1))],ℓ∈{0,1},\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dual}}=\mathbb{E}_{\ell\sim P(\ell)}\left[\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPSD}}(\mathbf{c}^{(\ell)},\mathbf{c}^{(\ell+1)})\right],\quad\ell\in\{0,1\}, (9)

where ℒOPSD​(𝐜S,𝐜T)\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPSD}}(\mathbf{c}^{S},\mathbf{c}^{T}) denotes the velocity-matching loss in Eq. (5), evaluated over student rollout 𝝉S∼𝒢𝜽​(𝐜(ℓ))\bm{\tau}^{S}\sim\mathcal{G}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{c}^{(\ell)}). This design enables the generator to progressively internalize spatiotemporal mechanics from dense simulations down to pure text inputs.

4.3.2 Controlled Physical Variation

While dual-level privilege bridges information densities, generators may still overfit to canonical motions rather than responding to physical parameter shifts. A key advantage of executable code is its capability to surgically perturb underlying parameters while holding other scene factors strictly invariant. PhysOPSD exploits this controllability to establish a causal physical contrast, explicitly exposing how physical shifts dictate dynamic consequences.

Controlled Variation Construction.

Given an executable scene parameterized by physical properties, denoted as W⁡(ϕ)W(\bm{\phi}), perturbing specific physical parameters ϕ\bm{\phi} constructs paired variants:

Wa=W⁡(ϕa),Wb=W⁡(ϕb).W_{a}=W(\bm{\phi}_{a}),\qquad W_{b}=W(\bm{\phi}_{b}). (10)

Typical perturbations adjust friction coefficients, restitution, object mass, initial velocities, or stiffness, while strictly preserving object geometries, camera trajectories, lighting, and initial compositions. Executing both scenes yields corresponding draft-prompt pairs:

(𝐩a,𝐝a),(𝐩b,𝐝b).(\mathbf{p}_{a},\mathbf{d}_{a}),\qquad(\mathbf{p}_{b},\mathbf{d}_{b}). (11)

Crucially, the grounded prompts 𝐩a\mathbf{p}_{a} and 𝐩b\mathbf{p}_{b} explicitly describe the contrasting physical conditions, ensuring that the text-only student possesses sufficient semantic context to distinguish differing physical behaviors during deployment.

Paired On-Policy Rollout.

To decouple the causal impact of physical variation from generative stochasticity, both variants share an identical initial Gaussian noise:

𝐱1a=𝐱1b∼𝒩⁡(𝟎,𝐈).\mathbf{x}_{1}^{a}=\mathbf{x}_{1}^{b}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}). (12)

The student executes independent on-policy rollouts under their respective conditioning:

𝝉aS∼𝒢𝜽​(𝐜aS,𝐱1a),𝝉bS∼𝒢𝜽​(𝐜bS,𝐱1b),\bm{\tau}_{a}^{S}\sim\mathcal{G}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{c}_{a}^{S};\mathbf{x}_{1}^{a}),\qquad\bm{\tau}_{b}^{S}\sim\mathcal{G}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{c}_{b}^{S};\mathbf{x}_{1}^{b}), (13)

and is optimized over each rollout trajectory via:

ℒvar=12​[ℒOPSD​(𝐜aS,𝐜aT)+ℒOPSD​(𝐜bS,𝐜bT)],\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{var}}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPSD}}(\mathbf{c}_{a}^{S},\mathbf{c}_{a}^{T})+\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPSD}}(\mathbf{c}_{b}^{S},\mathbf{c}_{b}^{T})\right], (14)

where each branch naturally integrates the dual-level privilege hierarchy from Eq. (9). Shared initial noise purely suppresses task-irrelevant rollout variance, making paired responses more directly comparable.

In summary, PhysOPSD leverages the intrinsic abstraction and controllability of executable code to internalize spatiotemporal physics and dynamic causality into the generator weights. At inference, all simulation components and physical drafts are discarded, leaving a general T2V or TI2V generator 𝐯𝜽​(𝐱t,t,𝐩,∅)\mathbf{v}_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{t},t,\mathbf{p},\emptyset) with zero runtime overhead.

5 Experiments

In this section, we conduct experiments to answer the following research questions: (RQ1) Does PhysOPSD improve physically plausible video generation? (RQ2) Does executable code provide effective privileged supervision? (RQ3) How do structured privileges improve learning?

5.1 Experimental Settings

Baselines.

We apply PhysOPSD to two unified video generators, OmniWeaving [30] and UniVideo [43]. As a post-training method, our primary comparisons are against the respective base models to directly measure capability gains. Since prior physics-oriented post-training methods are built on disparate backbones, we additionally implement three representative baselines: PhyT2V [45] for test-time scaling, SFT using WISA [42], and PhysHPO [5] for offline RL. We also report results from advanced video generators for reference, while further examining OPSD variants in our ablation studies. Details of baselines are in Appendix B.

Evaluations.

We evaluate PhysOPSD across two complementary aspects: ➀ physical plausibility, adopting VideoPhy-2 [3] for T2V and PhyGround [24] for TI2V to assess law-specific physical adherence; and ➁ general video quality, employing VBench [11] to measure general visual fidelity and semantic alignment.

Implementation Details.

PhysOPSD optimizes student LoRA parameters using AdamW with a constant learning rate of 1×10−51\times 10^{-5}, weight decay of 0.010.01, and gradient clipping at 1.01.0. Teacher weights are updated via an exponential moving average with a decay of 0.99990.9999 after paired gradient aggregation. Each student trajectory uses K=20K=20 rollout denoising steps. Training employs BF16 mixed precision on NVIDIA H20 GPUs. At deployment, the student generates videos without teacher or simulation guidance.

5.2 Main Results

To answer RQ1, we conduct comprehensive evaluations of PhysOPSD on physical and general generation benchmarks in Table 1, complemented by qualitative baseline comparisons (Figures 14 and 15) and diverse generative showcases (Figures 5, 16 and 17). Observations are summarized below:

Obs.❶ PhysOPSD consistently improves physical plausibility across backbones with high sample efficiency, while preserving general video quality. As shown in Table 1, PhysOPSD achieves top physical adherence across both UniVideo (13B) and OmniWeaving (8.3B), boosting VideoPhy-2 overall scores by +4.2+4.2 and +4.1+4.1, and PhyGround by +1.6+1.6 and +3.4+3.4, respectively, with physical commonsense (PC) reaching 4.614.61. Crucially, PhysOPSD achieves these gains using only 33K samples, markedly outperforming SFT (8080K) and offline RL (2121K). Meanwhile, this physical specialization incurs no catastrophic forgetting: VBench confirms that PhysOPSD maintains or even slightly improves overall visual quality and text alignment (e.g., UniVideo rises from 83.583.5 to 84.084.0, while OmniWeaving remains steady at 83.383.3), verifying that on-policy distillation protects foundational visual representations.

Obs.❷ PhysOPSD generates physically faithful dynamics over baselines and generalizes robustly to visually rich, open-domain scenes. In Figures 14 and 15, baselines exhibit motion stagnation, severe geometric distortions, or broken reflection mechanics during concrete leveling and teapot rotation, whereas PhysOPSD synthesizes continuous, physically consistent interactions. Furthermore, although physical drafts in PhysOPSD-Engine use simplified simulation geometry, the learned dynamics transfer robustly to open-domain photorealistic scenes (Figures 5, 16 and 17), successfully capturing fluid sloshing, impact cratering, elastic penetration, and optical reflection. This verifies that PhysOPSD internalizes transferable physical mechanics rather than overfitting to synthetic simulation appearances.

5.3 Analysis of Code-as-Privilege

To answer RQ2, we compare different privileged modalities under an identical budget of 33K samples, as shown in Figure 6: (i) vanilla model (w/o Privilege); (ii) declarative prompt expansion (w/ Refined Text); (iii) real reference videos (w/ Real Video); and (iv) executable simulation drafts (w/ Coding Draft). We give the following insights:

Obs.❸ Executable code serves as an effective privileged context for physically plausible video generation. As shown in Figure 6, refined text (w/ Refined Text) yields negligible physical gains and slightly decreases VideoPhy-2 All (62.862.8 vs. 62.962.9), showing that declarative descriptions cannot ground spatiotemporal mechanics. Meanwhile, real reference videos (w/ Real Video) produce only marginal improvements (63.163.1 vs. 62.962.9), as complex background and visual clutter encourage the teacher to rely on visual shortcuts rather than transferable dynamics. In contrast, PhysOPSD (w/ Coding Draft) achieves decisive improvements, boosting PhyGround Overall to 68.368.3 (+3.5+3.5 over real video) and VideoPhy-2 All to 67.067.0 (+3.9+3.9 over real video). As qualitatively shown in Figures 4, 11, 12 and 13, PhysOPSD isolates pure dynamics from visual noise and enables parametric control, empowering the self-teacher with dense, physically faithful supervision.

5.4 Analysis of Structured Privilege

To answer RQ3, we further dissect the individual contributions of our two structural strategies under a controlled budget of 33K samples: dual-level physical privilege and controlled physical variation. Performance gains over the base model on VideoPhy-2 are illustrated in Figure 7. We summarize the following observations:

Obs.❹ Dual-level privilege smooths knowledge transfer via an intermediate information bottleneck. In Figure 7 (Left), while Abstract-Only (+2.6+2.6 on All) lacks complete geometric constraints and Dense-Only (+3.4+3.4) encourages visual shortcuts, our stepped hierarchy (Dual-Level) attains the highest gain (+4.1+4.1 on All). This confirms that abstract drafts effectively bridge the privilege gap to enable progressive dynamic internalization.

Obs.❺ Controlled physical variation exposes dynamic causality beyond learning from isolated scenes. In Figure 7 (Right), training on independent physical scenes without parameter-controlled variations (Independent-Only) achieves a +3.3+3.3 gain on All. In contrast, structuring data into paired variants differing by a single physical parameter (Controlled Pairs) elevates the gain to +4.1+4.1. This demonstrates that exposing explicit counterfactual dynamic shifts is far more effective for internalizing physical causality than merely observing standalone physical scenarios.

5.5 Analysis of Data Efficiency

Finally, we examine the data efficiency and scaling behavior of PhysOPSD by varying the training data budget from 11K to 44K instances. Performance gains are illustrated in Figure 8:

Obs.❻ PhysOPSD exhibits remarkable sample efficiency and steady scaling potential. As shown in Figure 8, with merely 11K samples, PhysOPSD yields an immediate improvement of +1.6+1.6 on All (+1.8+1.8 on PC≥4\text{PC}\geq 4). As the dataset scales to 44K, overall gains steadily increase to +5.1+5.1 (+3.8+3.8 on SA≥4\text{SA}\geq 4 and +2.8+2.8 on PC≥4\text{PC}\geq 4) without premature plateauing. Compared to traditional paradigms requiring tens of thousands of samples (e.g., 8080K for SFT and 2121K for offline RL), PhysOPSD leverages dense on-policy supervision from structured code privileges, delivering high sample efficiency and sustainable scaling performance.

6 Conclusion

In this work, we present PhysOPSD, a post-training framework that introduces executable code as privileged physical context for on-policy self-distillation. Recognizing that executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability, we develop PhysOPSD-Engine to construct verifiable simulation scenes and rendered drafts. PhysOPSD systematically translates these properties into dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose dynamic causality. Extensive experiments on standard physics benchmarks demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones with high sample efficiency, while preserving general video quality. We hope our code-as-privilege inspires future research on leveraging coding agents to empower generative models rather than replacing them, advancing physically grounded visual generation.

7 Scope of This Report

Algorithm over Monolithic Models.

PhysOPSD contributes a general on-policy self-distillation framework rather than delivering a single weight-locked model. This motivates our focus on relative capability gains over respective base generators (e.g., UniVideo [43] and OmniWeaving [30]) to confirm cross-architecture generalizability. Furthermore, our compact default budget of 33K samples highlights sample efficiency, while our scaling analysis (Section 5.5) confirms steady performance gains as data increases.

Empowering Rather Than Replacing Generation.

Central to our philosophy is leveraging coding agents to empower generative models rather than substituting them at test time. PhysOPSD-Engine is thus designed as an open, modular pipeline interfacing standard coding LLMs with physics engines. As foundational coding agents and physics solvers advance, the pipeline naturally inherits the ability to synthesize increasingly complex physical scenarios without altering the distillation formulation.

Boundaries of Simulation-Groundable Dynamics.

The physical scope of PhysOPSD is bounded by scenarios that standard simulation engines can stably compute: rigid-body contacts, elastic mechanics, and fluid dynamics. Chaotic multi-physics and thermodynamic phase transitions (e.g., combustion) are deliberately excluded due to solver instability and difficulty in isolating parameters. Rather than emulating all physical phenomena, our objective is establishing a principled blueprint for internalizing physical dynamics via code privilege.

Appendix A More Details of PhysOPSD

A.1 PhysOPSD-Engine Details

Synthesizing executable physical scenes requires translating abstract dynamic descriptions into syntactically valid and numerically stable simulation code. While frontier LLMs/VLMs exhibit proficient code generation and spatial reasoning, the non-linear nature of contact dynamics makes single-pass zero-shot generation unreliable for complex physical phenomena. To guarantee a verifiable physical basis, PhysOPSD-Engine combines a frontier coding agent with an automated execution-guided refinement loop.

Iterative Scene Refinement Workflow.

We adopt GPT-6-Astra as the backbone coding agent. Upon generating an initial scene program 𝒫\mathcal{P}, PhysOPSD-Engine executes it in the target backend (e.g., MuJoCo [39] or Blender [4]) and aggregates diagnostic feedback across three modalities: ❶ execution logs (e.g., syntax errors or solver convergence warnings), ❷ kinematic telemetry (e.g., penetration anomalies or constraint forces), and ❸ rendered preview keyframes. When physical implausibility, solver divergence, or poor camera observability is detected, the coding agent inspects the diagnostic trace to revise geometric configurations, contact parameters, or camera trajectories. This execution-observation-revision cycle iterates until all four verification criteria in Section 4.2 are satisfied.

Multi-Level Draft Generation.

To prevent dynamic discrepancies across privilege levels, dense drafts 𝐝dense\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}} and abstract drafts 𝐝abs\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}} for a given variant are rendered from an identical, frozen simulation state trajectory. Specifically, once a simulation execution succeeds, PhysOPSD-Engine records the full kinematic trajectory of all bodies and contact events. 𝐝dense\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}} is rendered with full surface meshes, material shaders, and realistic lighting, whereas 𝐝abs\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}} renders simplified wireframe primitives and centroid trajectories from the exact same camera viewpoint. This trajectory freezing guarantees that both privilege levels share identical underlying dynamics, completely eliminating confounding dynamic drift caused by re-simulation. For controlled variants, non-target attributes and initial conditions are frozen to isolate the causal parameter shift.

Outcome-Grounded Dual Prompt Annotation.

In the main text, we denote the target text condition uniformly as 𝐩\mathbf{p} for mathematical clarity. In practice, accommodating our omni-capable video generator entails producing two complementary text conditions via Qwen3-VL-32B [46], conditioned on the dense draft alongside a structured fact card containing measured physical telemetry:

  • •

    T2V Prompt: a self-contained description detailing the scene context, physical conditions, observable dynamic trajectory, and final state, used for deployment-time text-only student generation.

  • •

    V2V Instruction: an imperative prompt instructing the model to perform photorealistic visual refinement while strictly preserving the underlying spatiotemporal dynamics and spatial layout, shared by the teacher and draft-conditioned student.

Both text modalities are grounded strictly in the executed simulation telemetry rather than speculative prior descriptions. The concrete system prompts utilized for annotation are detailed below.

Effectiveness of PhysOPSD-Engine

To further validate the necessity of our agentic execution-guided loop, we compare PhysOPSD-Engine against a standard harness framework (i.e., Codex) using the identical backbone coding model (GPT-6-Astra). As illustrated in Figure 9, naive code generation without closed-loop simulation feedback frequently degenerates into non-physical shortcuts: collapsing into 2D schematic toy drawings without fluid mechanics (e.g., fluid pouring), omitting structural apparatus and floating in an ungrounded void (e.g., sponge compression), or approximating continuous 3D dynamics with simplistic line segments (e.g., transverse spring waves). In contrast, PhysOPSD-Engine leverages multi-modal execution diagnostics and kinematic telemetry to iteratively refine boundary conditions, contact constraints, and spatial geometry. This closed-loop refinement guarantees that the synthesized programs instantiate verifiable 3D physical environments with observable, physically grounded dynamics.

A.2 PhysOPSD-3K Statistics and Case Studies

Dataset Statistics.

PhysOPSD-3K comprises 33K total instances, encompassing base executable scenes alongside their derived multi-abstraction drafts (𝐝dense,𝐝abs\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{dense}},\mathbf{d}^{\mathrm{abs}}) and parameter-controlled paired variants (𝐝a,𝐝b\mathbf{d}_{a},\mathbf{d}_{b}). Distribution across domains are shown in Figure 10.

Case Studies.

Figures 11, 12 and 13 showcase qualitative case studies across each dynamic domain. By systematically perturbing underlying physical parameters (e.g., damping, gravity, stiffness, displacement, outlet radius, and stirring velocity), the self-teacher reliably synthesizes physically consistent dynamics under both dense geometric and abstract wireframe draft conditioning. These results confirm that code-derived privileges effectively isolate dynamic mechanics from visual noise, providing transferable physical guidance without appearance shortcuts.

A.3 PhysOPSD Algorithmic Overview

PhysOPSD unifies executable physical context construction via PhysOPSD-Engine and structured on-policy self-distillation. Algorithm 1 details the latter, taking the paired multi-level conditions constructed by PhysOPSD-Engine as input.

Appendix B More Details of Experiments

B.1 Baseline Implementations

Base Models.

We implement PhysOPSD on two unified video generation backbones: ❶ OmniWeaving [30], which supports interleaved multimodal conditioning and free-form composition, and ❷ UniVideo [43], a dual-stream architecture unifying video understanding, generation, and editing. Both models natively accommodate text and visual inputs, providing the foundation for asymmetric student-teacher conditioning without architectural modifications.

Baselines.

As a post-training framework, our primary evaluation focuses on assessing relative capability gains against the respective base models. Furthermore, because physics-oriented post-training methods for video generation remain relatively scarce and are typically coupled with disparate backbones, we select and adapt three baselines to represent three prevailing post-training paradigms onto the same backbones:

  • •

    PhyT2V [45]: an iterative test-time refinement strategy. We preserve its physical chain-of-thought reasoning and prompt revision workflow, adapting its generator to our respective base models for direct paradigm comparison.

  • •

    SFT [42]: standard supervised fine-tuning on physics-specific demonstrations. We fine-tune each base model on WISA-80K, which comprises approximately 8080K curated text-video pairs spanning 17 physical categories across dynamics, thermodynamics, and optics.

  • •

    PhysHPO [5]: an offline hierarchical preference optimization framework. We adopt its original 2121K curated real-world videos from OpenVidHD [29] as positive demonstrations, paired with base model rollouts as negative samples, tailored to OmniWeaving and UniVideo.

OPSD Variants.

For the privileged context analysis in Section 5.3, all variants are evaluated under an identical budget of 33K samples. ❶ For w/ Refined Text, we utilize the physical reasoning and prompt revision pipeline from PhyT2V on the real reference videos and their original prompts to synthesize enriched prompts with detailed physical descriptions, which serve as the privileged text context. ❷ For w/ Real Video, the teacher receives both the text prompt and raw reference videos as privileged context, supplemented using PhysHPO’s data selection pipeline to match the 33K budget.

B.2 Evaluation Benchmarks

VideoPhy-2.

VideoPhy-2 [3] evaluates action-centric physical commonsense across 200 action categories under the T2V setting. Following [42], we assess Semantic Adherence (SA) and Physical Commonsense (PC) by using GPT-5.5, reporting mean scores, the proportions of videos achieving SA≥4\text{SA}\geq 4 and PC≥4\text{PC}\geq 4, and the joint metric (All) satisfying both criteria simultaneously.

PhyGround.

PhyGround [24] benchmarks text- and initial-frame-conditioned generation (TI2V) across 250 diverse scenarios spanning 13 physical laws in solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, and optics. Following its official benchmark protocol, we evaluate General plausibility (covering temporal coherence and object permanence) and law-specific Physics compliance, reporting their equal-weighted Overall score.

VBench.

We employ VBench 1.0 [11] to benchmark general video generation capabilities under the T2V protocol. Following the official evaluation suite across 16 fine-grained dimensions, we report normalized Quality, Semantic, and Total scores using standard prompt sets.
